completion_reason: Three material validation and safety decisions remain unresolved: upgrade recovery, evidence retention, and release acceptance proof.

questions.label: Failed upgrade recovery
questions.context: NexusCentral already stores durable state in SQLite and reports migration proof, but the production rollback promise is not defined. A rollback means returning the application and its stored-data format to the last known
questions.evidence: `adapters/runtime-adapters/src/sqlite-store.mjs` stores snapshots, events, and host values in SQLite WAL, while `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` reports migration proof without stating what happens if a production upgrade fails after accepting new work.
questions.impact: An upgrade failure must not corrupt accepted work or silently erase activity created after the upgrade began.
questions.question: What must survive a failed upgrade?

choices.text: Restore software and preserve accepted work
choices.consequence: The release must support compatible rollback or forward data repair, increasing migration effort but protecting every acknowledged run and conversation.
Recovery is simpler, but work accepted after the snapshot may be lost and operators must be warned before upgrading.
No downgrade path is maintained, reducing compatibility work but making a broken upgrade dependent on an emergency fix.

questions.recommendation_reason: This matches the recorded requirement that NexusCentral, rather than clients or models, owns crash-safe accepted work.

questions.label: Evidence retention
questions.context: Run evidence is immutable, meaning it cannot be edited after completion, but immutability does not decide whether an authorized operator may eventually delete it. A deletion marker is a small permanent record showing who
questions.evidence: `services/nexus-node/src/run-coordinator.mjs` returns canonical run, result, experiment, and artifact records; `packages/contracts/index.mjs` defines terminal run states; and the planned Runs tab owns immutable evidence, artifacts, validation, and approvals. None of the supplied boundaries defines retention or deletion.
questions.impact: Unlimited evidence growth can exhaust storage, while silent deletion can destroy accountability and reproducibility.
questions.question: When may completed run evidence be removed?

choices.text: Policy expiry with a deletion marker
choices.consequence: Authorized retention rules may remove artifacts after holds expire while preserving hashes, approval history, and an audit record of the deletion.
Evidence remains until a deliberate action, improving control but requiring ongoing storage management and manual cleanup.
Reproducibility is strongest, but storage grows without bound and long-lived deployments become harder to operate safely.
Storage is predictable, but important investigations or approvals may lose supporting material unless exported first.

questions.recommendation_reason: It preserves immutable accountability while fitting the recorded need to enforce resource ceilings in a long-running multi-user deployment.

questions.label: Release acceptance
questions.context: Current checks cover many technical paths, but the new six-tab product and several production boundaries do not yet have a single release sign-off rule. Human-view proof means an operator completes realistic tasks in the
questions.evidence: `docs/12-IMPLEMENTATION-STATUS.md` reports domain-kit, integration, scale, LM Studio, Playwright, Electron-survival, migration, and Codex-harness checks, while also listing interrupted replay, trusted-LAN certificates, real cloud credentials, and other unproven areas. `apps/web/app/page.jsx` still shows the old five-tab shell rather than the approved six-tab surface.
questions.impact: A release can pass component checks yet still fail an operator during recovery, approval, or an end-to-end task.
questions.question: What proof makes a production release ready?

choices.consequence: Every claimed production path must pass automated checks, restart-recovery scenarios, and human-view workflows before an operator explicitly signs off.
Releases can ship faster when checks pass, but interaction failures and confusing recovery behavior may reach production.
A limited production pilot supplies real-world evidence, but early operators knowingly carry risks not eliminated before launch.

questions.recommendation_reason: It confirms the provisional direction of full automatic validation followed by manual review and matches the existing emphasis on service-survival and human-view proof.
